principal_component_head.summary: Principal components of the training span's feature rows, fitted without labels; a small supervised head reads the component scores.
principal_component_head.implementationNote: Bridge: PCA (full SVD) of the train-span feature rows, labels unread; a logistic head (or gradient boosting) on the component scores gives P(up), ridge gives the price. Differs from the spec: PCA predicts nothing, so a supervised head is added, the only part that reads labels (principal-component regression). Expect: components keep variance, not direction, so a small predictive axis can be dropped; edge near a plain logistic regression at best.

component_count.label: Component count
component_count.description: How many principal components are kept (capped at the feature count).

whiten_components.label: Whiten components
whiten_components.description: Divide each component score by its deviation so every component has unit variance.

head_model.label: Head
head_model.description: What reads the latent code: linear (logistic regression for P(up), ridge for the price) or gradient boosting (200 small histogram trees). The only part of the model that sees labels.

regularization_strength.label: Head regularization strength
regularization_strength.description: Inverse L2 penalty of the linear head (C of the logistic regression, 1/alpha of the ridge); larger trusts the code more.

native.produces: A ranked set of perpendicular directions in feature space, the share of feature variance each one carries, and for every bar a short vector of scores giving the position of its centred feature row along the leading directions, from which the row can be approximately rebuilt.
native.targetVariable: The feature row of a bar: its coordinates along the few directions in which the feature rows vary the most, with no statement about the next move.
native.objectiveNote: Principal component analysis solves the rebuild problem in closed form: the directions that keep the most variance are the same directions that lose the least when a row is flattened onto them and rebuilt, so no iterative training is needed.

metrics.why: On the rows it was fitted on the kept directions lose exactly one minus their explained variance share, so the real test is whether rows from a later span, flattened onto the same directions and rebuilt, lose about the same share or noticeably more.
metrics.baseline: Rebuilding every unseen row as the training mean of each feature, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: When two directions carry nearly the same variance their order and orientation can swap from one fit to the next, so a component can be read as a market factor only if the same loading pattern returns across folds once sign is aligned.

The directions are ranked by variance and not by usefulness, so a downstream predictor on the scores has to be compared with the same predictor on all the raw features to see whether a small predictive direction was thrown away with the low-variance ones.
metrics.baseline: The same downstream predictor on the raw feature rows of the same bars.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes one input series before modelling and says nothing about how much variance the kept directions carry.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This belongs to fractional differencing of an input series; the projection reads each row alone and keeps no memory.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The projection forms no groups, so a measure of how tight and separate clusters are never applied to it.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively nothing about direction is predicted; a hit rate appears only when a supervised head is placed on the component scores.

notApplicable.name: Component independence
notApplicable.why: The component scores are only uncorrelated, which is weaker than independent, and the method makes no promise beyond zero correlation.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter takes the leading principal components of the training span's standardised feature rows by a full singular value decomposition without reading labels, then feeds each bar's component scores to a logistic regression (or gradient boosting, by the head dial) that is the only part to see the up or down labels, which is principal component regression; every as-run number therefore measures that supervised head reading the scores and none of them measures how much variance the components keep.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the output of an unweighted, ridge-penalised logistic regression (or a histogram gradient boosting classifier when the head dial says so) fitted on the training rows' principal component scores, standardised with the training scores' own mean and deviation, with no calibration curve afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows the mean squared error of rebuilding the standardised feature rows from the kept principal components, in squared standardised feature units; on validation rows the head's logarithmic loss in nats per bar; one value each for the single fit

meaningful.why: The head on the component scores is an unweighted likelihood fit, so the logarithmic loss on test bars is the honest score of the odds it states, read against the loss of quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.
The components were kept for carrying variance and not for predicting, so this tests whether the high-variance directions happen to order up bars above down bars once the head reads the scores.
A bounded second opinion on the head's stated odds that a few confident misses cannot dominate, useful because a few variance directions often leave the head close to the base rate.

The head is fitted without class weights and without a curve fitted on validation rows, so comparing its stated probability with the observed up share is a fair test of the head's own scale on the component scores.

A bin-free check of whether the head's log-odds on the component scores are too bold or too timid on test bars, which matters most when the boosting head is chosen and can overfit a short score vector.

If the predictive direction was dropped with the low-variance components the head answers almost the same probability on every bar, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up shows that at a glance.
The hit rate of the head's up or down call at even odds, read against the fold's training majority class because the unweighted head leans toward whichever class was commoner in training.
It shows whether the head on the component scores calls both directions or has settled on the commoner training class, which plain accuracy would hide on a trending fold.
One symmetric number for the head's hard calls that stays at zero when the component scores lead the head to call a single direction on every bar.
What the head's direction call earned after costs under the engine's trading rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds because the components were ranked by variance and not by direction.
Net profit of the head's calls per unit of bar-to-bar swing under the engine's rule, which only the side of one half that the head's probability falls on can move.
The deepest hole the head's calls dug under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, describing the path of the traded calls and not the projection.
Winning dollars over losing dollars of the closed trades that the head's flips produced, read with the trade count because a head near the base rate may rarely flip.
The share of closed trades from the head's calls that ended positive after costs, a description of the engine's exit rule applied to this head and not a score of the components.

A second fit of the same projection with a ridge (or boosting) head on the component scores forecasts the size of the move, and this tests whether that principal component regression beats predicting no change on the same resolved bars.
The typical miss in points of the ridge head's move forecast from the component scores, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same resolved bars.
How often the sign of the ridge head's move forecast matched the realised move; it comes from the separate price fit and need not agree with the traded call of the logistic head.
The search over component count and head choice is scored by the engine's trading objective on inner training blocks, so this is an optimistic selection score to read beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The head is fitted without class weights, so its probability tracks the training base rate and the balanced score would grade it against a prior it was never trained toward.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the projection or the head produced.

The training curve holds the error of rebuilding the standardised feature rows from the kept components and the validation curve holds the head's logarithmic loss, two different quantities, so their difference measures nothing.

caveats: Components keep variance and not direction, so a small predictive axis can be dropped with the low-variance components and the head can at best match a plain logistic regression on the same features.
The explained variance share of the kept components is written to the fit summary for the training rows only; no rebuild error on validation or test rows is recorded.
The fit report's training figure is the rebuild error of the standardised feature rows and its validation figure is the head's logarithmic loss, two different quantities that must not be compared.

The price forecast comes from a second, separately fitted copy of the projection with a ridge head trained on a move target clipped at the training rows' own first and ninety-ninth percentiles, so it can disagree with the traded direction call.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

independent_component_head.summary: FastICA unmixes the training span's feature rows into statistically independent sources, fitted without labels; a supervised head reads the sources.
independent_component_head.implementationNote: Bridge: FastICA (negentropy contrast) on train-span feature rows, labels unread; the sources, a fixed linear map of a bar, feed a logistic head (or boosting); ridge for the price. Differs from the spec: a supervised head is added; non-convergence is logged. Expect: the sources span the same subspace as PCA with the same count, so the linear head gives nearly PCA's answer; only the boosting head uses their independence.

component_count.label: Component count
component_count.description: How many independent sources are unmixed.

head_model.label: Head
head_model.description: What reads the latent code: linear (logistic regression for P(up), ridge for the price) or gradient boosting (200 small histogram trees). The only part of the model that sees labels.

regularization_strength.label: Head regularization strength
regularization_strength.description: Inverse L2 penalty of the linear head (C of the logistic regression, 1/alpha of the ridge); larger trusts the code more.

native.produces: An unmixing matrix and, for every bar, a short vector of source values obtained by multiplying the centred and whitened feature row by that matrix, where the sources are made as statistically independent of each other as a linear map allows.
native.targetVariable: The feature row of a bar: the values of the hidden, mutually independent sources whose linear mixture is assumed to have produced that row, with no statement about the next move.
native.objectiveNote: The fixed-point version described in the specification reaches independence by making each unmixed source as far from a bell curve as possible through an approximation of negentropy, after whitening has already removed plain correlation.

metrics.why: The unmixing matrix is chosen so the sources stop sharing information on the rows it was fitted on, and the claim worth testing is that the same matrix still yields sources with almost no mutual information on rows it never saw.
metrics.baseline: The same pairwise mutual information measured on the whitened rows before unmixing, which are uncorrelated but not yet independent.

metrics.why: The sources come out in no fixed order and with arbitrary sign, and when the features are close to bell-shaped the unmixing rotation is not pinned down at all, so a source counts as real only if a matching one reappears after sign and order are aligned across refits.

A downstream predictor reading the unmixed sources should be compared with the same predictor reading the whitened rows before the rotation, because that isolates what the independence step added beyond decorrelation.
metrics.baseline: The same downstream predictor on the whitened principal component scores of the same rows.

metrics.why: The fixed-point iteration stops when the unmixing matrix barely changes between sweeps or when the iteration limit is hit, and an unmixing matrix taken at the limit is a half-finished rotation whose sources should not be interpreted.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes one input series before modelling and says nothing about whether the unmixed sources are independent.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This belongs to fractional differencing of an input series; the unmixing matrix reads each row alone and keeps no memory.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The unmixing produces continuous source values and no groups, so there are no clusters whose tightness could be scored.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The sources carry equal variance by construction and are unordered, so a per-source variance share is not a property of this model.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: The rotation to independent sources is invertible, so the rebuild error measures only the whitening step's truncation and not the independence the model is about.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively the unmixing predicts nothing about direction; a hit rate appears only when a supervised head is placed on the sources.

non_negative_factorization_head.summary: NMF learns additive parts of the shifted training feature rows without labels; each bar's non-negative activation of those parts feeds a supervised head.
non_negative_factorization_head.implementationNote: Bridge: NMF (coordinate descent) factorises the train-span rows into frozen parts; a bar's code is its exact non-negative least-squares activation, read by a logistic head (or gradient boosting); ridge for the price. Differs from the spec: z-scores are shifted to be non-negative with train-fixed constants; a supervised head is added, the only part that reads labels. Expect: parts of shifted z-scores are not natural parts; edge near the base rate.

component_count.label: Component count
component_count.description: How many non-negative parts are learned.

head_model.label: Head
head_model.description: What reads the latent code: linear (logistic regression for P(up), ridge for the price) or gradient boosting (200 small histogram trees). The only part of the model that sees labels.

regularization_strength.label: Head regularization strength
regularization_strength.description: Inverse L2 penalty of the linear head (C of the logistic regression, 1/alpha of the ridge); larger trusts the code more.

native.produces: A small set of non-negative part vectors over the features and, for every bar, a non-negative activation per part, so that adding the parts in those amounts approximately rebuilds the bar's non-negative feature row.
native.targetVariable: The non-negative feature row of a bar: how much of each learned additive part is present in it, with no statement about the next move.
native.objectiveNote: Because both the parts and their activations are forbidden to go below zero, a row can only be built by adding parts and never by cancelling one against another, which is what makes the parts readable as ingredients.

metrics.why: The factorisation is fitted to make parts times activations match the training rows, so the honest test is how much of the feature variance is lost when unseen rows are rebuilt from the frozen parts with activations solved by non-negative least squares.
metrics.baseline: Rebuilding every unseen row as the training mean of each feature, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: The factorisation has many equally good solutions and the answer depends on the starting point, so a part can be read as a market ingredient only if a matching part shows up again when the fit is repeated on another fold or from another start.

A downstream predictor reading the part activations should be compared with the same predictor reading the raw feature rows, which shows whether squeezing the rows into a few additive parts kept or threw away what matters.
metrics.baseline: The same downstream predictor on the raw feature rows of the same bars.

metrics.why: The alternating updates of parts and activations stop when the rebuild error barely changes or when the iteration limit is reached, and parts taken at the limit are an unfinished fit whose shapes should not be interpreted.

manifold_embedding_head.summary: Isomap or locally linear embedding unfolds the training span's feature rows into a few coordinates without labels; a supervised head reads the coordinates.
manifold_embedding_head.implementationNote: Bridge: Isomap (geodesic kernel MDS) or LLE on an evenly spaced train-span subsample, labels unread; the head learns from the fitted coordinates and a new bar is placed by the estimator's out-of-sample map. Differs from the spec: fitted on a subsample (quadratic memory); a supervised head is added, the only part that reads labels. Expect: a few coordinates of a noisy feature cloud; edge near the base rate.

manifold_method.label: Manifold method
manifold_method.description: Isomap (geodesic distances) or locally linear embedding (local reconstruction weights).

neighbor_count.label: Neighbor count
neighbor_count.description: Nearest neighbours that define the local graph.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: Evenly spaced training bars the manifold is fitted on (memory grows with its square).

head_model.label: Head
head_model.description: What reads the latent code: linear (logistic regression for P(up), ridge for the price) or gradient boosting (200 small histogram trees). The only part of the model that sees labels.

regularization_strength.label: Head regularization strength
regularization_strength.description: Inverse L2 penalty of the linear head (C of the logistic regression, 1/alpha of the ridge); larger trusts the code more.

native.produces: A few coordinates per bar that flatten the curved cloud of feature rows, either by keeping shortest-path distances along the neighbour graph (Isomap) or by keeping each row's recipe as a blend of its nearest neighbours (locally linear embedding), with no direction call and no rebuilt input.
native.targetVariable: the position of each bar's feature row on a low-dimensional surface fitted to the feature rows themselves; it is not a statement about any future price
native.objectiveNote: Isomap asks straight-line distances in the map to equal shortest-path distances walked along the neighbour graph, and locally linear embedding asks each mapped point to stay the same weighted blend of its neighbours, and both are solved by an eigen-decomposition in one pass, so there is no loss curve to watch.

metrics.why: It checks that bars sitting side by side in the unfolded map were also neighbours among the original feature rows, so a shortcut edge in the neighbour graph did not glue two unrelated market states together.
metrics.baseline: the same method on the same held-out rows with only the neighbour count changed

metrics.why: Isomap's whole objective is that straight-line distances between mapped points reproduce the shortest-path distances walked along the neighbour graph, so one minus the squared correlation between those two sets of distances is the method's own fit measure and shows how much of the graph's geometry a few coordinates could not hold; it applies to the Isomap setting only.
metrics.baseline: the same graph distances set against the straight-line distances among the original feature rows, which shows how much curvature the unfolding had to remove

metrics.why: Locally linear embedding chooses its coordinates to minimise how far each mapped point sits from the blend of its neighbours' mapped points under the weights learned among the feature rows, so the cost left over is the method's own quality measure; it is read only for the neighbour count and coordinate count it was solved with, and it applies to the locally linear embedding setting only.

It checks the opposite failure: feature rows that were close before unfolding should still be close afterwards, which is what Isomap promises through its graph distances and locally linear embedding promises through its blending weights.
metrics.baseline: the same method on the same held-out rows with only the neighbour count changed

metrics.why: The eigenvectors that become the coordinates can swap order or flip sign when the training span moves, so this counts how often each coordinate reappears after matching; a coordinate that does not recur means something different on every refit.

It compares a reader fed the unfolded coordinates with the identical reader fed the untouched feature rows, which shows whether flattening the cloud kept or discarded whatever the features knew about the next move.
metrics.baseline: the same head fitted on the raw standardised feature rows of the same folds

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes a time series, while the unfolding treats the feature rows as an unordered cloud and produces no series whose stationarity it claims.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This belongs to fractional differencing of a price series; a neighbour graph over feature rows keeps or loses neighbourhoods, not price memory.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The methods output coordinates and never assign a bar to a group, so there are no clusters to grade until a separate clustering step is added on top.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: Variance explained is the yardstick of a straight-line projection; these methods bend the space on purpose, so the share of variance kept says nothing about whether neighbourhoods survived.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively the unfolding predicts nothing, so a hit rate exists only after a supervised reader is bolted onto the coordinates.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error

metrics.why: The second term of the training loss charges the encoder for moving its Gaussian code away from the standard normal prior, and reading it apart from the reconstruction term shows whether the bound is being earned by using the code or by ignoring it.

metrics.why: Natively the same negative lower bound is computed on training rows and on validation rows, so a validation value well above the training value means the encoder and decoder have memorised the training rows instead of learning where rows in general fall.

The specification's generative use is decoding draws from the standard normal prior into new rows, and this ratio shows whether those decoded rows are fresh or are near copies of rows the decoder was trained to rebuild.
metrics.baseline: The same nearest-training-row distance measured for real rows held out of training.

metrics.why: The decoder can turn draws from the standard normal prior into new rows, and the share of those decoded rows that land inside the neighbourhood of real held-out rows shows whether the draws look like market feature rows at all, which the copying ratio alone cannot show because a decoder that outputs one blurred average row is far from every training row and still passes it.
metrics.baseline: The same neighbourhood share measured for real held-out rows against the training rows.

metrics.why: Real held-out rows are only reproduced if the decoded prior draws spread over every kind of row the training rows contain, so the share of real rows that fall inside the neighbourhood of the decoded rows exposes a decoder that covers one mode of the feature rows and ignores the rest.
metrics.baseline: The same coverage share measured for a second set of real held-out rows in place of the decoded rows.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: The model's native score is its own lower bound on the log probability of unseen rows, and a transport distance between sampled and real return distributions belongs to path simulators rather than to a density of the feature row.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No reference embedding network for market rows exists to compute a Fréchet distance in, and the stamped table invented the metric without a definition the engine or the registry could follow.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: Uniformity is a target for contrastive embeddings on a sphere, while this latent code is regularised toward a standard normal prior and checked by the count of active latent units instead.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively the encoder and decoder never see an outcome label and predict no direction, so a hit rate exists only after a runnable bridge adds a readout that reads labels.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A density model of a data row takes no position, so a return per unit of risk describes the Model Cycle's trading rule applied to the bridge's call and not the variational autoencoder itself.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter trains the variational encoder and decoder on the training span's feature rows with the negative evidence lower bound and a warmed-up divergence weight, reading no label, then fits a logistic regression (or gradient boosting, by the head dial) on the posterior means and calls up or down by averaging that head over seeded draws from each bar's posterior; nothing is generated and no likelihood bound is reported, so every as-run number measures the supervised head reading the latent code and none of them measures the density model.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the mean, over the configured number of draws from the bar's Gaussian posterior seeded by the run seed and the bar's row, of an unweighted logistic regression (or histogram gradient boosting classifier) that was fitted on the training rows' posterior means, with no calibration curve afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: mean squared error in standardised feature units

meaningful.why: The head is an unweighted likelihood fit and its answer is averaged over posterior draws, so the logarithmic loss on test bars is the honest score of the odds that averaging states, read against the loss of quoting the fold's training up share.

It tests whether the latent code that the divergence charge pulled toward the prior still orders up bars above down bars once the head reads it, the only route by which the label-free model can help a direction call.

A bounded second opinion on the averaged odds, useful here because averaging the head over posterior draws pulls uncertain bars toward one half and the squared miss rewards that honesty without the logarithm's sensitivity.

Because the head is fitted without class weights and without a curve fitted on validation rows, comparing the averaged probability with the observed up share is a fair test of whether the posterior averaging left the scale right.
The head is fitted on posterior means but asked about noisy draws, which shrinks its log-odds, so the slope shows whether that shrinkage made the stated odds too timid on test bars.
A wide posterior or a collapsed code makes the averaged head answer almost the same probability on every bar, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up shows that at a glance.
The hit rate of the averaged head's up or down call at even odds, read against the fold's training majority class because the unweighted head leans toward whichever class was commoner in training.
It shows whether the head on the latent code calls both directions or has settled on the commoner training class, which plain accuracy would hide on a trending fold.
One symmetric number for the head's hard calls that stays at zero when a collapsed latent code leads the head to call a single direction on every bar.

What the averaged head's direction call earned after costs under the engine's trading rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds because the latent code was trained to explain rows and never to find direction.
Net profit of the head's calls per unit of bar-to-bar swing under the engine's rule, which only the sign of the averaged probability of up minus one half can move.
The deepest hole the head's calls dug under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, describing the path of the traded calls and not the quality of the latent code.
Winning dollars over losing dollars of the closed trades that the head's flips produced, read with the trade count because an averaged head near one half can flip often and pay costs each time.
The share of closed trades from the head's calls that ended positive after costs, a description of the engine's exit rule applied to this head and not a score of the encoder.

A second fit of the same variational autoencoder with a ridge head on the posterior mean forecasts the size of the move, and this tests whether that forecast beats predicting no change on the same bars.
The typical miss in points of the ridge head's move forecast from the posterior mean, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same resolved bars.
How often the sign of the ridge head's move forecast matched the realised move; it comes from the separate price fit and need not agree with the traded call of the averaged logistic head.

The search over latent size, hidden size, divergence weight and head choice is scored by the engine's trading objective on inner training blocks, so this is an optimistic selection score to read beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The head is fitted without class weights, so its probability tracks the training base rate and the balanced score would grade it against a prior it was never trained toward.

The training curve is the rebuilding error of a row decoded from a noisy posterior draw and the validation curve is the rebuilding error decoded from the posterior mean, and neither holds the divergence term, so their difference is not an overfit measure of the bound that was minimised.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the encoder or head produced.

caveats: The encoder epoch that is kept is the one with the lowest rebuilding error of the posterior mean on the validation rows' features, a choice the checkpoint enumeration has no value for and one that ignores the divergence term; no direction score selects anything and the head has no checkpoint.

The loss curves show squared rebuilding error only, so the evidence lower bound that the optimiser minimised and its Kullback-Leibler term are never logged and the model's native score cannot be read from the run.
The divergence weight rises linearly over the warm-up epochs, so early epochs minimise a different mix of the two terms from later ones while competing for the same kept-epoch choice.

The head is fitted on posterior means but predicts by averaging over noisy posterior draws, which pulls uncertain bars toward one half; with the linear head the price forecast uses the posterior mean exactly and is not averaged.
The price forecast comes from a second, separately fitted copy of the variational autoencoder with a ridge head, so it can disagree with the traded direction call.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

autoencoder_gan_fusion.summary: An autoencoder trained against two discriminators (one on the latent prior, one on generated rows) learns a code without labels; a supervised head reads the encoder's code.
autoencoder_gan_fusion.implementationNote: Bridge: encoder, decoder-generator, latent and data discriminators trained alternately on train-span feature rows (reconstruction + adversarial terms, labels unread); a logistic head (or gradient boosting) reads the frozen code. Differs from the spec: dense layers, generated rows unused for prediction; a supervised head is added, the only part that reads labels. Expect: adversarial losses are unrelated to direction; edge near a plain classifier.

latent_dimension.label: Latent dimension
latent_dimension.description: How many numbers the bottleneck code holds.

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units per hidden layer of the encoder and the decoder.

layer_count.label: Layer count
layer_count.description: Hidden layers in the encoder (the decoder mirrors it).

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.description: Share of hidden units switched off at random in training.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.description: AdamW step size of the encoder training.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.description: AdamW weight decay of the encoder.

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.description: Passes over the training span's feature rows.

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Epochs without a better validation reconstruction before training stops (the best epoch is restored).

adversarial_weight.label: Adversarial weight
adversarial_weight.description: Weight of the two generator losses against the reconstruction loss.

discriminator_steps.label: Discriminator steps
discriminator_steps.description: Discriminator updates before each encoder-decoder update.

head_model.label: Head
head_model.description: What reads the latent code: linear (logistic regression for P(up), ridge for the price) or gradient boosting (200 small histogram trees). The only part of the model that sees labels.

regularization_strength.label: Head regularization strength
regularization_strength.description: Inverse L2 penalty of the linear head (C of the logistic regression, 1/alpha of the ridge); larger trusts the code more.

native.produces: A compressed code for every input row, a rebuilt copy of that row from the code, and brand new rows drawn by pushing random prior noise through the same decoder, which a discriminator has been trained to tell apart from real rows.
native.targetVariable: The feature row itself: how closely the decoder rebuilds a real row from its code, and whether rows the decoder generates from prior noise are distinguishable from real rows.
native.objectiveNote: The fusion adds a reconstruction term to the forger-against-detective game, so the decoder is pulled toward rebuilding each real row while the discriminator pushes its output to look real, and the variational variant also adds a Kullback-Leibler pull of the code toward a Gaussian prior.

metrics.why: The fusion's own discriminator was trained inside the game and is therefore a biased referee, so a fresh classifier fitted after the decoder is frozen has to try to separate decoder-generated rows from unseen real rows, and landing near a coin flip means the decoder's samples pass.
metrics.baseline: A coin flip between real and generated, which is what a judge scores when the decoder's rows are indistinguishable from real rows of the same series.

metrics.why: The autoencoder half of the fusion promises that a row squeezed through the bottleneck code comes back nearly intact, and this measures on unseen rows how much of the feature variance the encoder and decoder pair loses.
metrics.baseline: Rebuilding every row as the training mean of each feature, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: The reconstruction term is added to the adversarial game precisely to stop the decoder from producing only a few kinds of row, so the share of real rows that have a generated neighbour tests whether that cure for collapsed variety worked.

The adversarial term is added to the autoencoder to cure blurry, averaged rebuilds, so the share of decoder samples that land inside the neighbourhood of real rows tests whether the discriminator's pressure made the samples realistic.

Because the decoder is trained to rebuild training rows exactly, it can pass the realism tests by replaying them, and comparing how close generated rows sit to training rows against how close held-out real rows sit exposes that copying.
metrics.baseline: The same nearest-training-row distance measured for held-out real rows of the same series.

metrics.why: Only the variational variant of the fusion has this term: it reports how far each row's code distribution sits from the Gaussian prior the decoder samples from, kept apart from the reconstruction term so one cannot hide the other.
A strong decoder under adversarial pressure can ignore parts of the code, so counting the code dimensions that still change from row to row shows how much of the bottleneck the fusion really uses.

The discriminator loss and the encoder-decoder loss rise and fall against each other, so their curves show only whether one side of the fusion overpowered the other and never how good the code or the samples are.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: The specification's discriminator plays the logarithmic real-versus-generated game, not the Wasserstein critic game, so the model never estimates this distance.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No pretrained market embedding network exists to compute a Fréchet distance in, so the generated rows are judged by the fresh-judge two-sample test, precision and recall instead.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: The code is pulled toward a Gaussian prior and not toward an even spread on a sphere, so uniformity is a goal of a different family of models.

notApplicable.name: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of a classifier trained on generated rows
notApplicable.why: The specification never trains a direction classifier on the decoder's generated rows and has no up or down label anywhere, so there is nothing for a ranking score to rank.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The adversarial half of the fusion defines no density for a row, and even the variational variant's bound is distorted by the discriminator term, so no honest likelihood figure exists.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter trains a dense encoder, a decoder that doubles as generator, a discriminator on the code and a discriminator on rows, all without labels, then freezes the encoder and fits a logistic regression (or gradient boosting, by the head dial) on the code to call up or down; the generated rows are never used for prediction, so every as-run number measures the supervised head reading the adversarially shaped code and none of them measures the quality of the generated rows.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the output of an unweighted logistic regression (or a histogram gradient boosting classifier when the head dial says so) fitted on the training rows' frozen encoder codes, standardised with the training codes' own mean and deviation, with no calibration curve afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: mean squared error in standardised feature units

meaningful.why: The head on the code is an unweighted likelihood fit, so the logarithmic loss on test bars is the honest score of the odds it states from the adversarially shaped code, read against the loss of quoting the fold's training up share.

It tests whether the handful of code numbers the encoder kept still order up bars above down bars once the head reads them, which is the only route by which the label-free fusion can help a direction call.
A bounded second opinion on the head's stated odds that a few confident misses cannot dominate, useful because a small code often leaves the head close to the base rate.
Because the head is fitted without class weights and without a curve fitted on validation rows, comparing its stated probability with the observed up share is a fair test of the head's own scale.
A bin-free check of whether the head's log-odds on the code are too bold or too timid on test bars, which matters when the gradient boosting head is chosen and can overfit a tiny code.
If the bottleneck code carries little about direction the head answers almost the same probability on every bar, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up shows that at a glance.
The hit rate of the head's up or down call at even odds, read against the fold's training majority class because the unweighted head leans toward whichever class was commoner in training.
It shows whether the head on the code calls both directions or has settled on the commoner training class, which plain accuracy would hide on a trending fold.
One symmetric number for the head's hard calls that stays at zero when the code leads the head to call a single direction on every bar.
What the head's direction call earned after costs under the engine's trading rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds because the code was never trained to find direction.
Net profit of the head's calls per unit of bar-to-bar swing under the engine's rule, which only the sign of the probability of up minus one half can move.
The deepest hole the head's calls dug under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, describing the path of the traded calls and not the fusion's code.
Winning dollars over losing dollars of the closed trades that the head's flips produced, read with the trade count because a head that rarely flips closes few trades.
The share of closed trades from the head's calls that ended positive after costs, a description of the engine's exit rule applied to this head and not a score of the code.

A second fit of the same encoder with a ridge (or boosting) head on the code forecasts the size of the move, and this tests whether that forecast beats predicting no change, which is the reference on the same bars.
The typical miss in points of the ridge head's move forecast from the code, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same resolved bars.
How often the sign of the ridge head's move forecast matched the realised move; it comes from the separate price fit and need not agree with the traded call of the logistic head.
Both curves hold the encoder and decoder's reconstruction error, so their gap shows whether the fusion memorised the training rows, though it says nothing about direction.

The search over code size, head choice and adversarial weight is scored by the engine's trading objective on inner training blocks, so this is an optimistic selection score to read beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The head is fitted without class weights, so its probability tracks the training base rate and the balanced score would grade it against a prior it was never trained toward.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the encoder or head produced.

caveats: The encoder epoch that is kept is the one with the lowest reconstruction error on the validation rows' features, a choice the checkpoint enumeration has no value for; no direction score selects anything and the head has no checkpoint.

The training and validation loss curves show reconstruction error of the encoder and decoder only; the adversarial terms that also drive the encoder update and the head's own loss are not in those curves.
The discriminator loss is kept only as a last-epoch figure in the fit summary and the decoder's generated rows are never judged, so no native sample-quality metric is measured for this run.
The price forecast comes from a second, separately fitted copy of the encoder with a ridge head, so it can disagree with the traded direction call.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.

siamese_network.summary: One weight-tied encoder embeds windows of bars so that windows with the same outcome sit close; a bar's forecast is the outcome share of its nearest training-span analogues.
siamese_network.implementationNote: Bridge: pairs are positive when the two windows share the up/down outcome (batch-hard triplet loss); the prediction is the distance-weighted outcome share of the nearest train-span analogues (price: their mean move). Differs from the spec: the index holds training windows only and never grows during the walk. Expect: analogues of a noisy window; edge near a nearest-neighbour classifier.

sequence_length.label: Sequence length
sequence_length.description: Bars in each window the encoder reads (fixed, never searched).

embedding_size.label: Embedding size
embedding_size.description: Numbers in each window's normalised embedding.

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units per hidden layer of the window encoder.

layer_count.label: Layer count
layer_count.description: Hidden layers of the window encoder.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.description: Share of hidden units switched off at random in training.

triplet_margin.label: Triplet margin
triplet_margin.description: How much closer a same-outcome window must be than the nearest other-outcome window.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.description: Windows per batch (the triplets are mined inside it).

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Epochs without a better validation log loss of the analogue readout before stopping.

native.produces: An embedding vector per window of bars and a distance between any two windows, and, by retrieving the nearest historical windows, the distribution of outcomes that followed those analogues.
native.targetVariable: Whether two windows of bars were followed by the same forward event, such as both touching the upper barrier first, stated as a distance that is small for same-outcome windows and large otherwise.
native.objectiveNote: One encoder with one set of weights embeds both members of a pair, and the contrastive or triplet loss pulls same-outcome windows together and pushes different-outcome windows apart only until a margin is cleared, with hard pairs mined inside each batch because easy pairs give no gradient.

metrics.why: The trader's question to this model is what followed the windows that look like this one, so the test is whether bars whose nearest analogues mostly went up are themselves followed by an up share above that of all scored bars, and likewise for analogues that mostly went down.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The share of up outcomes among a window's nearest analogues is a score per bar, and this shows whether the learned distance puts up bars next to past up windows often enough to order up bars above down bars.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value when the analogue share orders the bars no better than a coin.

metrics.why: The same analogue search can be run on the plain standardised windows with no encoder at all, and the trained distance earns its place only if its retrieval scores better than that raw nearest-window search.
metrics.baseline: The same nearest-analogue readout on the standardised windows without the learned embedding, on the same folds.

metrics.why: The analogue share is a counted frequency that can sit at zero or one when every retrieved window ended the same way, and a bounded squared-error score can grade such a share where a logarithmic score cannot.
metrics.baseline: Quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar of the same series.

metrics.why: Hard mining on a young embedding can pull every window onto one point or one line, where every distance is the same and retrieval is arbitrary, and the number of directions the embedding really uses on unseen windows exposes that.
metrics.baseline: The embedding size, the rank when every dimension carries its share.

metrics.why: The triplet or contrastive loss by step shows whether mined pairs still violate the margin or the encoder has run out of hard pairs, which is the only thing the loss curve of a distance learner can say.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian NLL Loss
notApplicable.why: The encoder is trained on a margin between distances and has no variance output, so a Gaussian likelihood of returns was never its objective or its output.

notApplicable.name: Volatility-Adjusted RMSE
notApplicable.why: The model learns a distance between windows and returns a set of past outcomes, not one forecast of the move whose error could be divided by volatility.

notApplicable.name: Top-Decile Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: The registry holds no metric restricted to the most confident slice of bars; the outcome separation by bin of the neighbour share already shows what the strongest analogue votes were followed by.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The share of retrieved analogues that went up is a count that reaches exactly zero or one when the neighbours all agree, and a logarithmic score of such a share is decided by those few bars.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian negative log-likelihood loss
notApplicable.why: The network outputs an embedding and a distance, never a mean and variance of the coming move, so there is no forecast density to score.

notApplicable.name: Root mean square error of a return forecast
notApplicable.why: Retrieval returns the set of outcomes that followed the analogues and the specification presents it as a distribution and not a point estimate, so a single-number forecast error is not its native measure.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter does what the specification's prediction step describes, a weight-tied encoder trained on the batch-hard triplet loss and read out by searching for the nearest analogues, so no supervised head stands in for the model as it does for the other members of this adapter. It differs in that two windows count as a pair when they share the plain up or down outcome, the encoder is a perceptron over the flattened window, and the index holds the fold's training windows only and never grows during the walk, so the as-run numbers measure analogues drawn from a frozen training span.
asRun.probabilityNote: Each bar's window is embedded by the frozen encoder, its nearest training windows up to the neighbour count are found by exact search, and the probability of up is their inverse-distance weighted share of up outcomes with a prior of one up and one down added, so the share can approach but never reach zero or one.

stepQuantity.unit: the training line is the batch-hard triplet hinge in units of distance between unit-length embeddings; the validation line is the logarithmic loss of the analogue readout in nats per bar

meaningful.why: The probability is a weighted share of up outcomes among the nearest training windows, a counted frequency and not a fitted likelihood, and the bounded squared-error score is the proper score for such a share, read against quoting the fold's training up share.

Inverse-distance weighting makes the analogue share vary smoothly from bar to bar, so this shows whether the triplet-trained distance places test windows near past windows with the same outcome often enough to order up bars above down bars.

The analogue share is never fitted to outcomes on validation bars, and the prior of one up and one down pulls it toward one half, so this slope shows whether a stronger analogue vote really means proportionally better odds.
The share is unweighted, so it should match the observed up share in each bin if the training analogues still describe the test bars, and the binned gap shows where the frozen index has gone stale.
If the embedding collapsed, every window retrieves an arbitrary mix of training windows and the share sits near the training up share on every bar, which this spread reveals.

The hard call is up when the weighted share of up analogues is at least one half, so the hit rate tests the majority vote of the retrieved training windows, read against calling every bar the fold's training majority direction.

A training span with more up windows than down windows tilts every neighbourhood toward up, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether the analogue vote calls both directions.

It gives one symmetric number for whether the majority outcome of the retrieved analogues moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the learned distance retrieves windows no more alike in outcome than chance.

It is the money made by going long when the weighted share of up analogues is at least one half and short otherwise under the engine's fill rule and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds.

It measures how steadily the analogue vote earned per bar after costs, and it is also the score the hyperparameter search steered the embedding size, triplet margin and neighbour count toward on training blocks.
It shows the deepest hole dug while following the analogue vote, which grows when the test bars move into conditions the frozen training index holds no close windows for.
It compares what the winning trades opened by the analogue vote made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read beside the trade count because a vote near one half flips often.
It counts how many trades opened when the analogue vote flipped ended in profit after costs, which describes the shape of the trading result and is not the direction hit rate.
It counts how often the weighted share of up analogues crossed one half, since a position is kept while the vote stays on one side, and every trading number of this model is read with it.
The vote inherits the up share of the indexed training windows, so a share of up calls far to one side shows the index's own imbalance is making the calls and not the distance.

The forecast line comes from a second encoder trained on triplets formed by the sign of the scaled move, whose forecast is the weighted mean move of its own nearest training windows, so this tests that second analogue search against forecasting no move.

It gives in points the typical miss of the mean move of the retrieved analogues, which averaging over many neighbours shrinks toward zero, read beside the miss of the no-change forecast on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the mean move of the second encoder's analogues, which come from a different embedding than the one behind the traded vote, so the two can disagree on a bar.

It is the selection score that chose the embedding size, hidden size, triplet margin, neighbour count and learning rate on training blocks, flattered by that choosing and shown only beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The analogue share is a smoothed count whose size is set by the neighbour count, the distance floor and the prior of one up and one down, not by a fitted likelihood, and it is also the quantity the kept epoch was chosen on, so its level does not grade the learned distance.
The readout carries no class weighting and is a counted share, so a logarithmic score that gives each class half the weight grades the odds on a footing they were never put on.
The prior of one up and one down keeps the weighted share strictly between zero and one, so this count is zero by construction for this adapter and says nothing about the neighbours.
The training curve holds the triplet hinge on distances and the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the analogue readout, so their difference compares two unrelated quantities.

With the long-only setting off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in the market describes the engine's rule and not the analogue vote.

caveats: The index holds the fold's training windows only and is never extended as the walk proceeds, so late test bars are matched against analogues that are a full test span old.

Triplets are mined from randomly drawn batches of training windows with no guard against an anchor and its positive having overlapping windows or overlapping forward horizons, so neighbouring bars can be matched on shared tape, which the specification warns against.
The kept epoch is the one whose analogue readout has the lowest logarithmic loss on the validation bars, so the validation loss is optimistic and only the test walk is out of sample.
The price forecast comes from a second encoder trained on triplets by the sign of the scaled move and kept on validation Huber loss, not from the direction encoder.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a simple binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
For any root other than MNQ the costs charged are the MNQ account figures applied as a stated assumption.
